author: reek
body: Bump-allocate `size` bytes aligned to `align` (a power of two) and zero them. The HBA reads these structures by DMA, so a stale byte is a real command; zeroing is not hygiene, it is correctness.

author: reek
body: Enable memory space (bit 1) and bus master (bit 2). Bus master is what lets the HBA write our buffer; without it the command completes and the buffer stays empty.

author: reek
body: A board can carry several SATA disks on one HBA; `ahci-find-nth` opens the n-th of them, counted in port order, so a caller choosing a MEDIUM (GopDisk's selection cells) can address each disk rather than whichever answers first.

author: reek
body: A port counts only when it is implemented, its PHY reports a device with communication established (SSTS.DET == 3), and its signature is a plain SATA disk (an ATAPI drive answers a different command set).

author: reek
body: Command header slot 0: five dwords of command FIS, one PRDT entry. Bit 6 of the first dword marks a write (host to device); a read leaves it clear.

author: reek
body: Wait for the command-issue bit to clear. A task-file error (IS.TFES) aborts the wait: the command failed and the buffer is meaningless.

author: val
body: The controller is found by PCI class 0x01 subclass 0x06; BAR5 is the HBA register block (ABAR). We enable memory space AND bus master (the HBA is a DMA master: it writes the sector into our buffer itself), set GHC.AE, pick the first port with a SATA drive present, stop that port, point it at a command list, FIS receive area, and command table we allocate and zero ourselves, restart it, then issue one READ DMA EXT through a single PRDT entry and poll the command-issue bit.

author: val
body: The firmware left the controller running, so stopping the port before repointing its registers is not optional -- an HBA reading a stale command list would DMA into memory that is now ours.

author: val
body: All register access is 32-bit: `peek-32`/`poke-32` are plain 32-bit moves, and an AHCI register must never be touched at another width. Every poll is fuel-bounded, so a wedged or absent controller returns a failure rather than hanging the boot.

author: val
body: A register host-to-device FIS carrying an ATA DMA-EXT command (`cmd`, 0x25 read / 0x35 write) for `count` sectors at `lba`, LBA48 addressing (device register 0x40). Dword 0 is FIS type 0x27 | C bit 0x8000 with the command in byte 2 (0x27 | 0x8000 = 32807). The count occupies bytes 12-13; a count of 0 means 65536 sectors to the drive, so callers must pass 1 or more.

author: val
body: One PRDT entry at command-table offset 128: the destination buffer and a byte count held as count-minus-one, with the interrupt-on-completion bit set. A single PRD covers up to 4 MB, so one entry carries the whole transfer -- the entire seed arrives in one command.

author: val
body: The port is quiesced again before EVERY return. The CLB, FB, and command table are per-call heap scratch: a port left running with FRE set retains DMA rights over them after the heap reclaims the addresses, and a late or asynchronous FIS -- or a fueled-out command a real drive completes seconds later -- then lands in whatever lives there next. Observed on real hardware (ASUS, live SATA drive) as a death mid welcome-fill at a depth that varied build to build; the Dell (internal drive disabled) and emulated AHCI never reproduce it.

author: val
body: IDENTIFY DEVICE (0xEC) is PIO data-in, but to the HBA it is one more command with a 512-byte data phase: the same FIS slot and the same single-PRD table carry it. The LBA and count fields of the FIS are not-applicable to the command and the device ignores them; count 1 sizes the PRD at the 512 bytes the device will send.
